description: Cross-binding SEMANTIC vectors. The crypto corpus in v1.json pins byte-identical hashing; this one pins the meaning of money. Every binding must agree with the Rust core on currency scale, on the exact decimal a value renders to, and on refusing malformed input. Each row exists because a real defect shipped past its absence -- see `why` on the category.

currency_decimals.why: A binding that hardcodes two decimal places mis-scales every zero-decimal and crypto currency. The WASM binding does exactly this (Money(i64) with SCALE=100), so JPY 1000 becomes 100000 minor units.

decimal_render.why: Money crosses the boundary as an exact decimal STRING. A binding that routes it through a float cannot reproduce these: it loses the value, the scale, or both. The Python wheel returned floats for 84 money fields until Sep 2026. Scale is part of the contract: addition keeps the widest operand's scale and multiplication sums them, so a binding that routes through a float cannot reproduce these strings even when the value happens to survive. Rows are raw decimal arithmetic. `money_scale_ok` marks the ones that are also valid as a USD AMOUNT: the engine refuses an input with more decimal places than the currency allows, which is the rule a binding with a hardcoded scale cannot express. Binding consumers should assert only the money-valid rows through a money path.

canadian_tax_rates.why: Every rate in the engine's table is a FRACTION, never a percentage. Quebec was written at the wrong scale and reported a 149.75% total rate; a $100 sale computed $149.75 of tax. Nothing pinned the value, so nothing caught it.

rows.note: HST replaces GST and PST in Ontario, so gst_rate is zero

rejected_inputs.why: A malformed value must be REFUSED, never coerced. Silently defaulting a bad currency to USD, or a bad id to the nil UUID, writes a record that points at nothing. Both shipped in the Node and Python bindings until Sep 2026.

accepted_inputs.why: The other half of the contract: tightening input parsing must not narrow what was already accepted. Case-insensitive currency codes and enum spellings stayed valid through the Sep 2026 strict-input work, and must stay valid.

money_scale_enforced.why: The engine refuses an amount with more decimal places than its currency permits: 0.005 is not a USD amount, and 0.5 is not a JPY one. A binding that hardcodes two decimal places cannot express this -- it accepts the JPY value and scales it wrongly. The WASM binding does exactly that (Money(i64) with SCALE = 100).
